title: Acid
content: An acid is a compound that dissolves in water to produce hydrogen ions, H+.
e: Acid is defined as follows. An acid is a compound that dissolves in water to produce hydrogen ions, H+. An acid produces hydrogen ions, H+, when it dissolves in water.

title: Dissociation reaction
content: A dissociation reaction is a chemical reaction in which a compound breaks apart into two or more parts.
e: Dissociation reaction is defined as follows. A dissociation reaction is a chemical reaction in which a compound breaks apart into two or more parts. Dissociation reaction is the idea that completes this fact.

title: Strong acid
content: Strong acid is an acid that completely dissociates in water and gives H+ ions.
e: Strong acid is an acid that completely dissociates in water and gives H+ ions. A strong acid dissociates almost completely in water. Here they want Strong acid.

title: Weak acid
content: Weak acid is an acid that partially dissociates in aqueous solution and gives H+ ions.
e: Weak acid is an acid that partially dissociates in aqueous solution and gives H+ ions. A weak acid dissociates only partly in water. Here they want Weak acid.

title: Alkali
content: An alkali is a base which is soluble in water producing OH- ions.
e: Alkali is defined as follows. An alkali is a base which is soluble in water producing OH- ions. An alkali is a soluble base that produces OH- ions in water.

title: Indicator
content: An indicator is a substance that has different colours in acidic and alkaline solutions.
e: Indicator is defined as follows. An indicator is a substance that has different colours in acidic and alkaline solutions. An indicator changes colour to show whether a solution is acidic or alkaline.

title: Neutralisation
content: Neutralisation is the reaction between an acid and a base to form a salt and water only.
e: Neutralisation is the reaction between an acid and a base to form a salt and water only. Neutralisation is acid plus base making salt and water.
